title: Complementary Classifier Induced Partial Label Learning

problem.claim: Partial label learning must disambiguate a set of candidate labels to identify the single valid ground-truth label for each training sample.

gap.claim: Existing partial label learning work does not fully investigate the effectiveness of complementary labels, which identify labels that do not belong to a sample.

contributions.claim: Uses non-candidate labels to induce a complementary classifier that forms an adversarial relationship with the traditional partial-label classifier to eliminate false-positive candidate labels.
Uses a dynamic graph based on a shared local topological structure between feature and label spaces to assist disambiguation.
Releases implementation code for the proposed approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on 4 controlled UCI data sets and 6 real-world data sets show superiority over state-of-the-art partial label learning methods.
The authors report that the experiments reveal the usefulness of complementary learning in partial label learning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Partial label learning associates each training sample with candidate labels, only one of which is valid.
The task is to disambiguate candidate labels and recover the ground-truth label.
Prior work has not fully examined complementary labels that exclude labels from belonging to a sample.
The approach induces a complementary classifier from non-candidate labels and uses dynamic graph structure to assist disambiguation.
Experiments across controlled UCI and real-world data sets are reported to outperform state-of-the-art partial label learning methods and show complementary learning is useful.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide the optimization objective, model architecture, or training procedure.
The names and characteristics of the 4 controlled UCI data sets and 6 real-world data sets are unspecified.
Quantitative results, evaluation metrics, and baseline configurations are not reported.
